==English==
{{was wotd|2007|February|21}}
{{wp|Negotiation}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|negociate}} {{qualifier|archaic}}

===Etymology===
c. 1598; {{bor+|en|la|negōtiātus|nocap=1}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|negōtior||to do business, trade}} (see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}), from {{m|la|negotium||business}} + {{m|la|-ō|-or|id=den}}, from {{m|la|nec||not}} + {{m|la|otium||leisure, ease, inactivity}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/nɪˈɡəʊ.ʃi.eɪt/|/nɪˈɡəʊ.si.eɪt/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/nɪˈɡoʊ.ʃi.eɪt/|/nɪˈɡoː.ʃi.eɪt/|a=Northern England}}
* {{IPA|en|/nəˈɡoʊ.ʃi.eɪt/|/nɪˈɡoʊ.ʃi.eɪt/|a=GA,CA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-negotiate.ogg|a=California}}
* {{IPA|en|/nɪˈɡəʉ.ʃi.æɪt/|/nɪˈɡəʉ.si.æɪt/|q2=uncommon|a=AU}}
** {{audio|en|en-au-negotiate.ogg|a=Queensland}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[confer]] with others in order to come to [[term]]s or reach an [[agreement]].
#: {{syn|en|treat|q1=formal, especially in order to reach a settlement|parley|q2=especially with an enemy}}
#* '''1963''', {{w|Martin Luther King, Jr.}}, to the eight fellow clergymen who opposed the civil rights action, "Letter from Birmingham Jail," ''Why We Can't Wait''
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[arrange]] or [[settle]] something by [[mutual]] [[agreement]].
#: {{ux|en|We '''negotiated''' the contract to everyone's satisfaction.}}
#: {{ux|en|The client and server computers must first '''negotiate''' a network protocol to be used.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-19|author=w:Timothy Garton Ash
|volume=189|issue=6|page=18|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/jul/10/geopolitics-transatlantic-trade-deal Where Dr Pangloss meets Machiavelli]
|passage=Hidden behind thickets of acronyms and gorse bushes of detail, a new great game is under way across the globe.{{...}}The current power play consists of an extraordinary range of countries simultaneously sitting down to '''negotiate''' big free trade and investment agreements.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[succeed]] in [[cope|coping]] with, getting over or navigating a hazard or obstacle.
#: {{ux|en|We '''negotiated''' the mountain track with difficulty.}}
#: {{ux|en|Although the car was quite rickety, he could '''negotiate''' the curves very well.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|author=Kevin Mitchell|title={{w|Roger Federer}} back from Wimbledon 2012 brink to beat {{w|Julien Benneteau}}|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/jun/29/roger-federer-wimbledon-2012-julien-benneteau|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161115072742/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2012/jun/29/roger-federer-wimbledon-2012-julien-benneteau|archivedate=15 November 2016|date=29 June 2012|passage={{w|Novak Djokovic}} earlier had '''negotiated''' his own tricky passage through the fifth day.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[transfer]] to another person with all the rights of the original holder; to [[pass]], as a [[bill]].
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[transact]] [[business]]; to carry on [[trade]].
#* {{RQ:Evelyn Diary|entrydate=June 1645|passage=Jews, Turks, Armenians,{{...}}'''negotiating''' in this famous Emporium.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To [[intrigue]]; to [[scheme]].
#* {{RQ:Bacon Henry 7|passage=Certaine it is, shee was a busie '''negotiating''' woman.}}
